[clinical_programs] grade_provisional. 56-year-old man with SOD1 c.341T>C p.(Ile114Thr), German tofersen early-access programme. Baseline CSF before treatment was unremarkable (normal protein, cell count, IgG, no oligoclonal bands). Injections 1-5 (days 1, 14, 28, 55, 84) were uneventful. Three days after the 6th injection (day 112; CSF that day 56 cells/uL, total protein 79 mg/dL, oligoclonal bands now positive) he developed generalised myalgia and restless legs, then progressive lower-limb paresis by days 122-124. MRI of the cervical and thoracic spine on day 126 showed low, partly punctiform contrast uptake and oedema consistent with myelitis; CSF then showed 37 cells/uL (lymphocytic), protein 119 mg/dL, CSF/blood IgM quotient 67.2 and positive CSF-specific oligoclonal bands; multiplex PCR for viral and bacterial agents was negative. Treated with intravenous prednisolone 1000 mg/day for 5 days (days 126-131) then an oral taper over 40 days: sensory symptoms and restless legs regressed rapidly but LEG WEAKNESS REGRESSED MUCH MORE SLOWLY -> partially_reversible. ;; source_ref_as_cited=PMID:38066205; doi:10.1007/s00415-023-12130-1

Read from DailyMed SPINRAZA SPL setid dd70cd5f-b0fc-4ba4-a5ea-89a34778bd94, version 21, effectiveTime 20260331 ('Revised: 3/2026'), fetched this session. Denominators are printed in the table header verbatim: 'SPINRAZA High Dose Regimen (Study 4) (N=50)' and 'Matched Sham Control (Study 1) (N=20)'. Dose is the High Dose Regimen, two 50 mg loading doses then 28 mg every 4 months (label Table 1, sec 2.1); dose_or_conc_value is set to the 50 mg loading dose, and the 28 mg maintenance dose is the other half of the same regimen. COUNT IS DERIVED, NOT PRINTED: the label prints percentages only; 6% of 50 = 3 patients and 0% of 20 = 0 patients, so '3/50 vs 0/20' is arithmetic and is marked implied. CONTROL IS NOT CONCURRENT: label sec 6.1 states verbatim that the comparator is 'historic-matched sham-control patients from Study 1', and the Table 4 header labels it 'Matched Sham Control (Study 1)'. Study 1 is NCT02193074 (the 12 mg infantile-onset sham-controlled trial), so the N=20 comparator is a matched SUBSET of that trial's N=41 sham arm - it is a historical external control, and the N=20 and N=41 control groups in this lane are NESTED, not independent. SHAM COMPARATOR CAVEAT: the sham procedure in Study 1 was a skin prick with no dural puncture, so any procedure-attributable event - procedural pain, post-lumbar-puncture headache, back pain - is systematically exaggerated by this comparison, because only the treated arm was actually punctured. Graded conservatively at 1 for that reason: transient, procedure-attributable, no evidence of parenchymal injury. DOSE CONTRAST, BOUNDED: procedural pain does NOT appear in Table 2 (the 12 mg infantile-onset table, N=80 vs sham N=41). That is NOT an incidence of zero - Table 2 lists only reactions occurring in at least 5% of SPINRAZA patients AND at least 5% more frequently or at least 2x as frequently as control, so all that can be said is that procedural pain fell below that threshold at 12 mg in the same population type. Do not read the absence as 0%. PATIENT OVERLAP - DO NOT SUM: Study 4 is NCT04089566 (DEVOTE) Part B, and its n=50 infantile-onset high-dose patients are the SAME 50 patients already represented in this dataset by CMS1304 (acquired_macrocephaly 1/50) from NCT04089566 and by CMS1589/CMS1597/CMS1600/CMS1603 from doi:10.1038/s41591-025-04193-6. notes: [dose_contrast_atlas] [dose_contrast_atlas] HEADLINE CNS FINDING OF THE ATLAS. Paper states verbatim: 'Radar-based analyses revealed broadly elevated AE rates across multiple clinical domains among gapmers, particularly within procedure-related and neurologic categories (Figure 4B)' and 'Within the i.t. subgroup, gapmers exhibited substantially higher AE rates than FM ASOs across multiple AE categories, including pronounced differences in procedure-related and neurologic domains (Figure 4BII), with corresponding WLS models demonstrating significant effect estimates.' readout_value=TBD BECAUSE THE MAGNITUDE IS PRESENTED ONLY AS A RADAR PLOT AND A COEFFICIENT PLOT - no numeric neurologic AE rate, numerator or per-category denominator is printed anywhere in the text, tables or supplementary tables (S1 is a source list, S2 the AE dictionary, S3 ASO metadata). Denominator available only at atlas level: 41,730 treated patients across 112 ASO treatments. Method is exposure-weighted weighted-least-squares regression at treatment level, so the unit of analysis is the ASO programme, not the patient. AUTHORS' OWN CAVEAT, which must travel with this row: 'Because nusinersen accounts for a substantial proportion of treated participants and is concentrated within the FM, 2'-MOE, and i.t. strata' they ran leave-one-out and equal-ASO-weighted sensitivity analyses, and conclude 'the gapmer-FM comparison is best viewed as an exposure-weighted clinical safety association rather than a definitive agent-independent class effect.' Graded 1, not 2: the readout is an aggregate clinical AE-category rate with no severity-resolved CNS event definition, no neuronal-injury biomarker and no imaging, so nothing in the rubric's grade-2 band (sustained neuroinflammation, treatment-emergent NfL rise, ventriculomegaly, or a specific clinically significant neurologic AE) is actually demonstrated. Severe-AE analyses were directionally consistent but were not resolved to the neurologic domain. RESTATES PRIMARY ROWS: this association is computed over a cohort that already includes nusinersen, tofersen, tominersen and n-of-1 ASOs held in this dataset from primary sources - it is a re-analysis of overlapping evidence, not independent evidence, and its patients must never be added to the per-oligo rows. grade_provisional

Lengths cluster around ~20 nt (Figure S2A), so the tested range is narrow and the null is correspondingly weak; absence of an association over a narrow range is not evidence of absence over a wide one. is_cns_specific=FALSE because this analysis is over ALL AEs across all routes, not a CNS-compartment readout - it is filed as a design-predictor negative, not as a CNS measurement, and must not be counted as a CNS observation. THIS IS THE MOST IMPORTANT CAVEAT IN THE WHOLE ATLAS FOR CNS WORK, and it applies to every SafeSense row in this lane: intrathecally delivered ASOs are given almost exclusively to patients with severe neurologic disease, so route, indication and disease severity are collinear by construction. The authors say so plainly: 'SafeSense also does not fully separate ASO-associated AEs from procedure-related events or manifestations of the underlying disease... We therefore interpret these patterns as reflecting an indication - ASO interaction rather than isolated drug toxicity alone. Systematic placebo-based or natural-history correction was not feasible because many sources lacked appropriate comparator groups.'
